text: 📊 New Feature Proposal: Session Tracking for slack-hq

text.text:
*Problem*: We need chronological tracking of agent development activities in slack-hq to maintain verifiable session details and follow progress across multiple agents.

*Inspiration*: Based on the sophisticated session management in the claude md project, which provides comprehensive lifecycle tracking.

*Key Features*:
• `/session` slash command suite (status, history, start, stop, show, post)
• JSON-based session persistence
• Slack channel integration via Council Bot
• Multi-agent coordination support
• Lifecycle hooks for automatic tracking

*Architecture*:
• Session data: `.claude/data/sessions/*.json`
• Commands: `.claude/commands/session/*.md`
• Hooks: Session lifecycle automation
• Slack: Auto/manual posting to #council-ops

*Implementation Roadmap*:
:one: *Phase 1* (2-3 days): Basic persistence - session data storage
:two: *Phase 2* (3-4 days): Slash commands - CLI interface
:three: *Phase 3* (2-3 days): Slack integration - Council Bot posting
:four: *Phase 4* (2 days): Status line - realtime tracking

*Documentation*:
• Full spec: `docs/specs/session-tracking.md`
• Research report: `docs/research/session-tracking-analysis.md`
• GitHub issue: <https://github.com/IkechukwuAbuah/slack-hq/issues/2|#2 Session Tracking>

*:speech_balloon: Council Feedback Requested*:
1. Priority ranking (high/medium/low)?
2. Which agent wants to implement Phase 1?
3. Should session updates auto-post or manual only?
4. Any architectural concerns or suggestions?

*Success Metrics*:
• 80%+ agent adoption within first month
• 100% of active sessions produce JSON entries
• Average 1+ Slack update per active sprint
• 90%+ handoffs include notes/activities
